 White Sox To Trade Davis Martin, Luis Castillo To Rockies
 By Anthony Franco |
 at November 19, 2026 6:41pm CDT 
 6:41pm: Rookie southpaw  Sean Sullivan is one of the players going to Chicago, reports Mark Feinsand of MLB.com . Francys Romero reports that teenage catcher  Douglas Veliz is also going to Chicago.
 6:37pm: The White Sox are trading starting pitchers  Davis Martin and  Luis Castillo to the Rockies, reports Jeff Passan of ESPN . Colorado is sending two prospects the other way. The Rox are absorbing Castillo’s $22.75MM salary for the upcoming season as a means of enticing Chicago to part with Martin.
 It’s a big investment for a Colorado team starved for starting pitching. Martin is the centerpiece of the deal from their perspective. The Texas Tech product has had an inconsistent career but pitched at a roughly league average level over the last couple seasons. Martin has made 55 appearances over the last two years, pitching to a 4.02 earned run average across 288 2/3 innings.
 A 14th-round pick in 2018, Martin debuted four years later. He was up and down from Triple-A as a rookie and then underwent Tommy John surgery, preventing him from establishing himself until 2025. Martin performed at a back-end level that year, posting a 4.10 ERA with a modest 17.3% strikeout rate over 26 appearances. He missed a month midseason with a forearm strain.
 Martin won a camp battle to secure a spot in Will Venable’s season-opening rotation in 2026. He was one of the biggest early-season stories in the American League, pitching at an ace level through the end of May. Martin reeled off 67 2/3 innings with a flat 2.00 ERA while striking out 27% of opponents over his first 11 starts. He seemed ticketed for an All-Star berth and was in some early conversations as a dark horse Cy Young candidate.
 The wheels fell off once the calendar turned to June. Martin allowed 5.63 earned runs per nine over his final 78 1/3 innings. His early-season strikeout rate was cut in half, as he only punched out 14.4% of batters faced the rest of the way. His fastball velocity, which was in 94-95 mph range for the first couple months, dropped a tick. The swing-and-miss rates on his curveball, cutter and slider all plummeted from early-season levels.
 The truth lies somewhere between the extremes. Martin’s early-season run of dominance was inflated by a soft schedule. He carved up the Angels a couple times and had some of his best games against bad offensive teams in Toronto, Seattle and Kansas City. His late-season work isn’t exactly representative of his true talent either, as Martin was hampered physically. He missed a couple weeks in August due to blister troubles and pitched through a right calf issue in the second half.
 Martin finished the season with a 3.95 ERA while establishing a new career high with 146 innings. He struck out 19.8% of opponents against a solid 7.5% walk percentage with roughly average whiff and ground-ball rates. Martin’s overall performance was that of a league average starter — just with a wildly up-and-down road to get there.
 The 29-year-old righty (30 in January) immediately becomes Colorado’s best starting pitcher. He has between two and three years of service time and has yet to qualify for arbitration. Martin is under club control for four seasons under the current collective bargaining setup. (If MLB succeeds in getting the union to budge on a salary cap, it’d probably come with five-year free agency for players in their 30s, which would shrink Colorado’s control window by a season.) Martin also has an option remaining and can still be sent to the minors if things go off the rails, but the Rockies clearly anticipate he’ll be a key rotation piece for the next few seasons.
 Castillo is also a lock to begin the year in Colorado’s rotation. His acquisition is more the cost of doing business to acquire Martin, however. Castillo wouldn’t come close to a $22.75MM salary if he were a free agent this winter. The Rockies are taking him on primarily for salary relief purposes, even if they’ll also count on him as a veteran source of innings.
